    Binary biproduct squares #

    This file records generic categorical properties of binary biproducts. A biproduct map factors through the maps obtained by changing one summand at a time, and the squares obtained by adjoining an identity summand are pushouts or pullbacks. The biproduct of two cokernels is the cokernel of the biproduct of the two morphisms (CategoryTheory.Limits.CokernelCofork.isColimitBiprod); this is the biproduct analogue of Mathlib's CategoryTheory.Limits.CokernelCofork.isColimitTensor. For functors preserving zero morphisms, biproduct preservation is stable under composition and follows from preservation of products and coproducts of the same shape. The short complex of a mapped commutative square agrees with the mapped short complex through the canonical biproduct comparison.

    In a category with zero morphisms, a zero object and binary biproducts give all finite biproducts (LargeIndecomposable.Foundations.hasFiniteBiproducts_of_hasBinaryBiproducts), and a biproduct indexed by Option J splits off its none summand (LargeIndecomposable.Foundations.biproductOptionIso); the latter is the inductive step for computing additive invariants of finite biproducts. Similarly, LargeIndecomposable.Foundations.biproductSumIso splits a sum-indexed biproduct into its two indexed parts. An additive functor which kills one summand of a binary biproduct inverts the projection onto the other (CategoryTheory.Functor.isIso_map_biprod_fst_of_isZero). The biproduct comparison F.obj (X ⊞ Y) ⟶ F.obj X ⊞ F.obj Y is natural (CategoryTheory.Functor.biprodComparison_natural) and compatible with lifts. Unlike the Functor.mapBiprod lemmas, these statements need no preservation hypothesis. For a functor out of Cᵒᵖ, the comparison F.obj (op (X ⊞ Y)) ≅ F.obj (op X) ⊞ F.obj (op Y) through biprod.opIso has inverse given by the images of the projections (CategoryTheory.Functor.mapIso_biprod_opIso_trans_mapBiprod_inv).

      A category with zero morphisms, a zero object and binary biproducts has finite biproducts. Like Mathlib's CategoryTheory.Limits.hasBinaryBiproducts_of_finite_biproducts, this is a theorem rather than an instance, so that a concrete category may keep finite biproducts with better definitional properties.

          For a functor F out of Cᵒᵖ, the inverse of the comparison F.obj (op (X ⊞ Y)) ≅ F.obj (op X) ⊞ F.obj (op Y) through biprod.opIso is given by the images of the opposites of the projections.
